habitat: It roosts by day on a horizontal branch, up to about 20 m up, and also rests on the ground. Trees are an important part of the habitat. It is usually silent in the non-breeding range. Most records are of birds flushed by day or seen on roads at night.
summary: The only Palearctic nightjar on the Kruger list. The adult has greyish-brown upperparts with dark streaking, a pale buff hindneck collar and a white moustachial line. The closed wing is grey with buff spotting. The underparts are greyish-brown, with brown barring and buff spots. The bill is blackish, the iris dark brown and the legs brown. The male song is a sustained churring trill. SABAP1 says the first sightings are in September, arrival is mainly from late November, and most have left by late April.

similar.note: Fiery-necked Nightjar is the common woodland resident. European Nightjar is the Palearctic migrant and is usually silent while it is here.

head.pattern: Pale buff hindneck collar and a white moustachial line. Greyish-brown upperparts with dark streaking.

wings.pattern: Closed wing grey with buff spotting.

viewNotes.note: Greyish-brown and streaked, with a pale buff collar, resting lengthwise or on the ground.
White moustachial line and dark brown eye.
Streaked upperparts. The closed wing is grey with buff spots.
The upperwing pattern in flight was not named beyond the grey, buff-spotted closed wing.
Greyish-brown underparts with brown barring and buff spots.

calls.description: The male song is a sustained churring trill, sometimes for up to 10 minutes, often ending with a bubbling trill and wing-clapping. It is more frequent at dawn and dusk. SABAP1 says the species is usually silent in the non-breeding range, though Wikipedia says migrating or wintering birds sometimes sing. Grade A from Hankley Common, Surrey. The file also includes a flight call and wing-clapping. A South African file was grade E.

research.note: Status is a Palearctic migrant. Months are September to April, from SABAP1: first sightings in September, arrival mainly from late November, most gone by late April. Newman has no nightjar pages. Length is from Wikipedia (24.5–28 cm). The female song was not described. Chick down is not described beyond a young bird in a threat display. The call is grade A from England.
